Also label each option SAME, ADJACENT or ELSEWHERE against the root question, with a reason: SAME if it asks the root question or a sub-question of it, ADJACENT if it has the root's subject but asks a different question, ELSEWHERE if its subject is different. Decide the subject from the title and summary; count root_link only if the summary itself describes the root question's object of study. Do not add up the scores. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.

Criteria:
stakes: Suppose the question this option raises were answered, either way. 5 = a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) turns on the answer, and either answer would move it; 3 = the answer would refine a belief but no choice turns on it, or one answer is already much more likely than the other; 1 = either answer is already expected, or nothing would change. Do not score how famous or important is field, or closeness.
open: Has published work already measured how the answer changes with the quantity compute buys here (samples, ensemble members, resolution, model runs, model size, search width), across the range that $1,000 Lambda on-demand GPU (about 250 H100-hours) can reach? 5 = names the quantity and where published measurements stop (or that none exist), and the unmeasured range starts within that reach; 3 = the unmeasured range is reachable only through a smaller stand-in system, or published work already covers part of the reachable range; 1 = names no compute-bought quantity, or published work already covers everything within that reach, so open range lies only beyond it.
reshape: Does the option name a part of the work that one answer waits on step after step, and a reason those steps might not have to run in order? 5 = names that chain and roughly how long it is; one answer leaves most of a GPU idle (a small state, or few runs needed, so copies side by side would not fill it); names what would have to be true of the system for the steps to be computed at same time, in a form a cheap measurement could check; and no cited source already computes this chain in parallel for this system; 3 = names chain and way to restructure it, but one of these fails: answer needs many independent runs, so copies side by side already fill hardware; one run already fills a GPU; or no checkable condition named; 1 = sequential says none, or only parallelism is independent pieces (copies, a sweep, one job per GPU), or cited source already computes chain in parallel for this system. A method published for a different system does not lower. Do not score how famous method or field.
